text_note.zh: 本库文字和通行本（如《唐诗三百首》）有几处不同：“腰下实玦”通行本作“腰下宝玦”，“贤德北服南单于”通行本作“圣德北服南单于”，“慎勿疎”的“疎”通行本写作“疏”（同一个字）。这里用通行本。
text_note.en: The corpus differs from the commonly taught text (as in Three Hundred Tang Poems) in a few places. Where the corpus has shí jué, the taught text has bǎo jué (precious jade ring). Where the corpus has xián dé (worthy virtue), the taught text has shèng dé (sage virtue). The corpus also writes shū (careless) in an old variant form. We follow the taught text.

readings.en: In the place name Chang'an it is read cháng.
Wū dǐ means "inside the house"; read dǐ.

readings.zh: “乞为奴”是“请求做奴仆”，读 wéi。
readings.en: In qǐ wéi nú, "begging to become a servant", it is read wéi.

readings.zh: “且为王孙”是“姑且为了王孙”，读 wèi。
readings.en: In qiě wèi wáng sūn, "for the prince's sake", it is read wèi.

readings.zh: “隆准”指高鼻梁，“准”是鼻子，读 zhǔn。
readings.en: In lóng zhǔn, "a high-bridged nose", zhǔn means the nose.

readings.zh: “龙种”是皇家的后代，“种”读 zhǒng。
readings.en: In lóng zhǒng, "dragon seed", it is read zhǒng.
In cháng yǔ, "talk for long", it is read cháng.
In hǎo shēn shǒu, "fine fighting skill", it is read hǎo.

readings.zh: “单于”是匈奴等北方民族首领的称号，“单”读 chán。
readings.en: In chán yú, the title of a northern nomad chief, it is read chán.
Tuó tuó means camel; the first character is read tuó.

glosses.zh: 城头：城墙上面。
glosses.en: chéng tóu: the top of the city wall.

glosses.zh: 头白乌：白头的乌鸦，古人认为是不吉利的鸟。
glosses.en: tóu bái wū: a white-headed crow, which people of old thought was a bad omen.

glosses.zh: 延秋门：长安皇宫禁苑西边的门。唐玄宗逃离长安时，就是从这里出去的。
glosses.en: Yanqiu Gate: a west gate of the palace park in Chang'an. Emperor Xuanzong went out through it when he fled the city.

glosses.zh: 呼：叫。
glosses.en: hū: to cry out.

glosses.zh: 啄：用嘴叩、啄。
glosses.en: zhuó: to peck.

glosses.zh: 达官：地位很高的大官。
glosses.en: dá guān: high officials.

glosses.zh: 走避胡：逃跑躲避胡人的叛军。胡：这里指安禄山的军队。
glosses.en: zǒu bì hú: run away to escape the rebels. Hú here means An Lushan's army.

glosses.zh: 金鞭断折九马死：形容逃跑时非常慌张，鞭子都打断了，马也累死了。九马：一说指皇帝的好马。
glosses.en: jīn biān duàn zhé jiǔ mǎ sǐ: they fled in such panic that whips snapped and horses dropped dead. Jiǔ mǎ, "nine horses", is often taken to mean the emperor's fine horses.

glosses.zh: 骨肉：亲人，这里指皇帝的子孙亲属。
glosses.en: gǔ ròu: "bone and flesh", close family; here, the emperor's own relatives.

glosses.zh: 不待同驰驱：来不及等他们一起逃走。
glosses.en: bù dài tóng chí qū: there was no time to wait for them to flee together.

glosses.zh: 宝玦：珍贵的玉佩，形状像有缺口的圆环。
glosses.en: bǎo jué: a precious jade ring with a gap in it, worn at the waist.

glosses.zh: 青珊瑚：青色的珊瑚，也是贵重的佩饰。
glosses.en: qīng shān hú: blue-green coral, another costly ornament.

glosses.zh: 王孙：皇帝的子孙。
glosses.en: wáng sūn: a descendant of the emperor.

glosses.zh: 路隅：路边、墙角。
glosses.en: lù yú: a corner by the road.

glosses.zh: 乞为奴：请求让他做奴仆，只求活命。
glosses.en: qǐ wéi nú: begging to be taken as a servant, just to stay alive.

glosses.zh: 窜荆棘：在荆棘丛里东躲西藏。荆棘：带刺的灌木。
glosses.en: cuàn jīng jí: hiding here and there among thorn bushes.

glosses.zh: 完肌肤：完好的皮肤。
glosses.en: wán jī fū: unbroken skin.

glosses.zh: 高帝：唐高祖李渊，唐朝第一个皇帝。
glosses.en: gāo dì: Emperor Gaozu, Li Yuan, the first emperor of the Tang.

glosses.zh: 隆准：高鼻梁。传说汉高祖刘邦是高鼻梁，这里借来说皇家子孙相貌不凡。
glosses.en: lóng zhǔn: a high-bridged nose. Legend says Liu Bang, first emperor of Han, had one; here it means the royal family have noble faces.

glosses.zh: 龙种：皇帝的后代。古人把皇帝比作龙。
glosses.en: lóng zhǒng: "dragon seed", the emperor's descendants. The emperor was likened to a dragon.

glosses.zh: 殊：不同。
glosses.en: shū: different.

glosses.zh: 豺狼在邑龙在野：凶恶的叛军占了京城，皇帝却流落在外。豺狼：比喻安禄山叛军。邑：城，指长安。
glosses.en: chái láng zài yì lóng zài yě: the wolves (the rebels) hold the city, while the dragon (the emperor) is out in the wilds. Yì means the city, Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 千金躯：宝贵的身体。
glosses.en: qiān jīn qū: a body worth a thousand pieces of gold, a precious life.

glosses.zh: 临交衢：站在十字路口。交衢：四通八达的大路口。
glosses.en: lín jiāo qú: standing at a crossroads.

glosses.zh: 斯须：一会儿，片刻。
glosses.en: sī xū: a moment.

glosses.zh: 东风吹血腥：东风吹来血腥味，暗指叛军在长安杀人。
glosses.en: dōng fēng chuī xuè xīng: the east wind carries the smell of blood, a hint that the rebels are killing people in Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 橐驼：骆驼。叛军用骆驼运走抢来的财宝。
glosses.en: tuó tuó: camels. The rebels used camels to carry off their loot.

glosses.zh: 旧都：指长安，此时皇帝已经离开了它。
glosses.en: jiù dū: the old capital, Chang'an, which the emperor had left.

glosses.zh: 朔方健儿：北方的勇士。一说指哥舒翰在潼关打了败仗的唐军，一说指朔方节度使的军队。
glosses.en: shuò fāng jiàn ér: brave soldiers of the north. One view: the Tang army under Geshu Han that was crushed at Tong Pass. Another: the troops of the Shuofang command.

glosses.zh: 昔何勇锐今何愚：从前多么勇猛，现在怎么这样无能。
glosses.en: xī hé yǒng ruì jīn hé yú: once so brave and sharp, how can they be so useless now?

glosses.zh: 窃闻：私下听说。
glosses.en: qiè wén: I have heard in secret.

glosses.zh: 天子已传位：唐玄宗已经把皇位传给了太子，就是唐肃宗。
glosses.en: tiān zǐ yǐ chuán wèi: Emperor Xuanzong has passed the throne to the crown prince, who became Emperor Suzong.

glosses.zh: 北服南单于：在北方让少数民族首领归服。南单于：本是汉代南匈奴的首领，这里借指回纥（唐代北方的一个民族）的首领。
glosses.en: běi fú nán chán yú: in the north, the new emperor has won over a nomad chief. The Southern Chanyu was a Xiongnu chief in Han times; here it stands for the Uighur leader.

glosses.zh: 花门：山名，这里借指回纥。
glosses.en: huā mén: the name of a mountain; here it stands for the Uighurs.

glosses.zh: 剺面：用刀划破脸，是回纥等民族表示真心或悲痛的习俗。
glosses.en: lí miàn: cutting one's face with a knife, a custom of the Uighurs and other peoples to show sincerity or grief.

glosses.zh: 雪耻：洗去耻辱，这里指帮唐朝收复长安。
glosses.en: xuě chǐ: to wash away a shame; here, to help the Tang take back Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 慎勿出口他人狙：千万别把这些话说出去，怕有人暗中埋伏、偷听。狙：暗中窥伺。
glosses.en: shèn wù chū kǒu tā rén jū: be careful never to repeat this, for someone may be lying in wait to listen. Jū means to lurk and spy.

glosses.zh: 慎勿疏：千万小心，不要大意。
glosses.en: shèn wù shū: take care, do not let your guard down.

glosses.zh: 五陵：唐朝五位皇帝的陵墓，在长安附近。
glosses.en: wǔ líng: the tombs of five Tang emperors near Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 佳气：吉祥的气象，古人认为它表示国家会兴旺。
glosses.en: jiā qì: a lucky air or glow, which people of old believed showed the dynasty would prosper.

glosses.zh: 无时无：没有一刻不在，意思是唐朝一定会复兴。
glosses.en: wú shí wú: never for a moment absent; the dynasty will surely rise again.

translation.zh: 长安城墙上，有一只白头乌鸦，
translation.en: On the wall of Chang'an sat a white-headed crow;

translation.zh: 夜里飞到延秋门上不停地叫。
translation.en: at night it flew to Yanqiu Gate and cried and cried.

translation.zh: 它又飞到人家的大屋上去啄，
translation.en: Then it pecked at the roofs of great houses,

translation.zh: 屋里的大官们都逃走去躲避叛军。
translation.en: and the high officials inside fled from the rebels.

translation.zh: 金鞭打断了，好马累死了，
translation.en: Golden whips snapped, the fine horses fell dead;

translation.zh: 连皇家的亲骨肉都来不及带着一起逃。
translation.en: there was no time even to take the royal family along.

translation.zh: 一个人腰上挂着宝玉和青珊瑚，
translation.en: One young man wore a jade ring and blue-green coral at his waist:

translation.zh: 可怜这位王孙，在路边哭泣。
translation.en: a poor prince, weeping by the road.

translation.zh: 问他是谁，他不肯说出姓名，
translation.en: Asked who he was, he would not give his name;

translation.zh: 只说自己很苦，求人收他做奴仆。
translation.en: he only said how hard things were and begged to be taken as a servant.

translation.zh: 他已经在荆棘丛里躲了一百天，
translation.en: For a hundred days he had hidden among thorns,

translation.zh: 身上没有一块完好的皮肤。
translation.en: and not a patch of his skin was unhurt.

translation.zh: 高祖皇帝的子孙都是高鼻梁，
translation.en: All of Emperor Gaozu's descendants have high noses;

translation.zh: 皇家后代自然和平常人长得不同。
translation.en: the dragon's seed looks different from ordinary people.

translation.zh: 现在豺狼占了京城，皇帝流落在外，
translation.en: Now wolves hold the city and the dragon is in the wilds;

translation.zh: 王孙啊，你要好好保护自己宝贵的身体。
translation.en: prince, take good care of your precious life.

translation.zh: 我不敢在十字路口跟你多说，
translation.en: I dare not talk long here at the crossroads,

translation.zh: 只能为你停留一小会儿。
translation.en: but I will stand with you a moment for your sake.

translation.zh: 昨夜东风吹来一股血腥味，
translation.en: Last night the east wind carried the smell of blood;

translation.zh: 从东边来的骆驼挤满了旧都。
translation.en: camels from the east now crowd the old capital.

translation.zh: 北方的将士们本领那么高强，
translation.en: The soldiers of the north were so skilled;

translation.zh: 从前多么勇猛，现在怎么这样无能？
translation.en: once so brave and sharp, how can they be so useless now?

translation.zh: 我私下听说，老皇帝已经把皇位传给了太子，
translation.en: I have heard in secret that the old emperor has passed on the throne,

translation.zh: 新皇帝的威德让北方的回纥首领也归服了。
translation.en: and the new emperor's virtue has won over the chief of the north.

translation.zh: 回纥人划破脸面，请求帮唐朝报仇雪耻。
translation.en: The Uighurs have cut their faces and asked to help wash away the shame.

translation.zh: 千万别说出去，小心有人暗中偷听。
translation.en: Never repeat this; someone may be lurking to listen.

translation.zh: 可怜的王孙，千万小心，不要大意，
translation.en: Poor prince, be careful, do not let your guard down;

translation.zh: 五陵上的吉祥之气，从来没有消失过。
translation.en: the lucky glow over the Five Tombs has never faded.

background.zh: 唐玄宗天宝十四载（755年）冬天，安禄山起兵叛乱，这就是“安史之乱”。第二年六月，潼关失守，玄宗带着少数亲人从延秋门悄悄逃出长安，往四川去，很多皇家子孙来不及逃走。叛军进城后，杀了不少皇族的人。七月，太子在灵武（今宁夏一带）即位，就是唐肃宗。这年秋天，杜甫被叛军抓到长安，在城里看到一位落难的王孙，写下了这首诗。
background.en: In the winter of 755, An Lushan rose in revolt against the Tang. This is called the An Lushan Rebellion. In the sixth month of the next year, Tong Pass fell. Emperor Xuanzong slipped out of Chang'an through Yanqiu Gate with a few close relatives and headed for Sichuan, and many royal descendants were left behind. When the rebels entered the city, they killed many members of the royal family. In the seventh month, the crown prince took the throne at Lingwu (in today's Ningxia) as Emperor Suzong. That autumn Du Fu was captured by the rebels and taken to Chang'an. There he met a prince in hiding and wrote this poem.

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），唐代大诗人，人称“诗圣”。他的很多诗记下了安史之乱时老百姓和国家的苦难，所以被叫做“诗史”，就是用诗写成的历史。这首诗就是他被困在长安时亲眼所见，既同情王孙，又盼望朝廷早日收复京城。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was a great Tang poet, called the Sage of Poetry. Many of his poems record the suffering of ordinary people and of the country during the An Lushan Rebellion, so they are called "history in poems". This poem tells what he saw with his own eyes while trapped in Chang'an. He pities the prince, and he longs for the court to win back the capital soon.

appreciation.zh: 开头像一个阴森的电影镜头：夜里，一只白头乌鸦在城门上叫，又去啄大官家的屋顶，接着就是大官们慌忙逃跑，鞭子打断，马也累死，连皇家亲人都顾不上带。然后镜头停在路边：一个腰上挂着宝玉的年轻人在哭，他不敢说名字，只求做奴仆，身上全是伤。从前高高在上的王孙，现在比普通人还可怜。诗人不敢多说，却还是停下脚步，小声安慰他：叛军虽然凶，新皇帝已经即位，回纥也来帮忙，你千万要小心活下去，唐朝一定会复兴。整首诗像一场在街角匆匆进行的悄悄话，紧张、害怕，又带着一点希望。
appreciation.en: It opens like a creepy film scene. At night a white-headed crow cries on the city gate and pecks at the roofs of officials' houses. Then the officials flee in panic: whips snap, horses drop dead, and no one even waits for the royal family. Then the camera stops by the road. A young man with jade at his waist is crying. He dares not give his name, only begs to be a servant, and his body is covered in cuts. A prince who once stood so high is now worse off than an ordinary person. The poet dares not say much, yet he stops and whispers comfort: the rebels are fierce, but a new emperor is on the throne and the Uighurs are coming to help. Stay careful and stay alive; the dynasty will rise again. The whole poem feels like a quick, secret talk on a street corner: tense, frightened, but with a little hope.
